statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band well below the block threshold: NQ sits near a fresh overnight high, but ES and YM decline to confirm and Stress stays near the top of the elevated band on the unresolved energy, currency and rates backdrop.
recommendation: The deterministic Tail-to-action mapping resolves to EA_ON for NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD alike. A narrow danger window is flagged for the post-holiday U.S. cash reopening between 13:30 and 15:00 UTC, where a single auction discounts two sessions of accumulated Middle East, energy and rates news. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ extends to a fresh overnight high while ES stays flat, yields ease and a reported Hormuz shipping understanding caps the energy channel
body: U.S. cash equity markets were closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day and reopen at 13:30 UTC today, so the Nasdaq-100 last settled a full cash session on 4 September. NQ futures trade at 29,739.00, up 173.75 points or 0.59% from the 29,565.25 previous close, and have extended the overnight band to 29,525.00-29,749.75. Price now sits roughly 11 points below a high it set within the last hour, which is the single mild Tail amplifier in this window. It is not accompanied by the rest of a pathological path: the 225-point overnight band has already produced two-way trade, including a retracement from the earlier 29,722.75 high, and there is no shallow-pullback sequence, no failed-retracement chain and no repeated extension. Cross-asset confirmation is contradictory rather than merely absent. S&P 500 e-mini futures are at 7,722.75, up 0.01%, inside a 7,698.50-7,728.50 band, and Dow futures are lower, so the three U.S. index futures disagree on direction. The Asian session explains the split: South Korea's Kospi rallied close to 2% on broad-based buying while the Nikkei managed 0.07% as the yen strengthened below 153.00 to a six-month high on Bank of Japan tightening expectations, reinforced by revised second-quarter GDP and strong July wage data ahead of the 17-18 September meeting. That is a semiconductor and technology bid, not an index-wide directional bid. Treasury yields have eased, with the 10-year near 4.78% after a 1.6 basis point decline and the 2-year at 4.37%, so rates are not pressuring equity multiples in this window. VIX at 14.95 is a last-cash-session reading from before the holiday and shows no volatility bid. The Stress side is where the risk sits, and it has become two-sided since the previous assessment. Brent at $97.51 and WTI at $92.96 remain near three-month highs after the weekend U.S.-Iran tanker exchange and the second strike in a month on Saudi Aramco's Jizan refinery, but the pace of the advance has slowed to well under half a percent, and Iran's foreign ministry said on Monday that an understanding with Oman to manage Strait of Hormuz shipping is days from completion and would be documented with the International Maritime Organization. Brent briefly reversed to $96.15 on that report. The understanding is genuinely two-sided: it could restore tanker throughput, and it could also provoke a U.S. response to Iranian control of transit decisions. Today's U.S. calendar is light, with NFIB at 10:00 UTC, NY Fed consumer inflation expectations at 15:00 UTC, a 3-year auction at 17:00 UTC and consumer credit at 19:00 UTC, and the week's Tier-1 releases are PPI on Thursday and CPI on Friday, both at 12:30 UTC. The one genuine structural feature of the next 24 hours remains the 13:30 UTC cash reopening, where a single auction must discount two sessions of accumulated news, and that is where the narrow danger window is placed.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours were published continuously with Tail between 5 and 10 and the mapped state green throughout. Stress ran in the mid-50s through the Asian and European hours of 7 September, then stepped into the low-to-mid 60s from about 14:00 UTC as the weekend U.S.-Iran escalation and the Aramco Jizan report carried crude to multi-week highs, and it has held there since. Confidence fell from the mid-80s to the mid-70s across the Labor Day cash closure, when no U.S. breadth or volume evidence was being generated, then recovered steadily into the low 80s overnight as Asian trade supplied a live price path again. The dominant mode alternated between normal and mixed and at no point in the window registered persistent directional efficiency.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour path is shaped by one dominant scheduled feature, the U.S. cash reopening at 13:30 UTC after the Labor Day closure, where a single auction must discount two sessions of accumulated Middle East, energy and rates news. Conditional Tail is held in the low double digits through the Asian and European hours, rises through the U.S. pre-market to a path peak of 17 in the first full hour of cash trade, then decays through the afternoon on the assumption that price discovery becomes orderly and retracements occur, without being decayed through the 20:00 UTC closing auction. Conditional Stress follows the same shape, entering the high band from 10:00 UTC and easing back into the elevated band after the cash close. Every hour maps to EA_ON because no persistent no-retracement structure is observed and cross-asset signals conflict rather than align. The stated conditional invalidation is repeated extension above 29,749.75 after failed retracements, with ES, YM, yields and crude turning in the same direction; that combination is absent at the assessment cutoff and would need to be observed before the published afternoon decay could be treated as valid.
